Objective: Investigate food origin in the Raised Food Garden using measurable evidence and explain how production decisions affect food quantity, quality or handling.
Materials: Journal, labels, ruler/tape, balance where available, clean containers, tally sheet, calculator, handwashing supplies.
DIY: Use locally available baskets, clean reused food-grade containers, handmade labels, paper process cards and simple balances/measuring vessels where suitable.
Steps: 1. Frame a question about food origin. 2. Select samples. 3. Measure or classify evidence. 4. Record quantities and quality observations. 5. Trace the product through at least four farm-to-food stages. 6. Explain one risk, loss point or improvement.
Evidence: Data table plus process sequence, calculation or evidence-based explanation.
Challenge: Recommend one practical change that could improve quality, handling efficiency or reduce loss.
Safety: No tasting unless the school has separately approved a supervised food activity. Wash hands before and after handling produce. Use only clean, teacher-approved samples and containers. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and any processing machinery.
